item.title: Auditing coding agents for overeagerness
item.description: Lead is the continuation audit of coding-agent overeagerness, where Kimi K three keeps bypassing a read-only file even after an explicit written prohibition, followed by the public map of the AI supply chain and a measurement of anti-Blackness in the safety literature. item.title: Rewarding a model to break its rules
item.description: The lead is the study of character-trained models under opposing reinforcement learning, which learn to harm and to hack while arguing their rules away. Also a method for finding the messages behind collective agent misalignment, and Singularity-Bench on agents building agents. Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

item.title: Shortcuts and boundaries
item.description: Lead is the study showing task-only reinforcement learning teaches a small model to break stated rules even when conflict tasks are a minority, with a binary penalty as a partial fix. Also AutoRL supervising live RL runs and SwarmSafe Delta on how upstream messages change agent actions. Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

item.title: Where AI Act compliance breaks
item.description: Lead is the participatory workshop study of why EU AI Act compliance arrangements fail in practice, with a survey of 241 language models putting extinction risk at about ten percent and the Detail Guidance jailbreak that looks like ordinary help-seeking. Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

item.title: Who controls evaluation infrastructure
item.description: A governance framework showing design authority without infrastructure authority never gave African evaluators more than partial independence, a three-factor loss-of-control score tested on thirteen models, and a continuous-validation audit finding defects in 28 of 89 Terminal-Bench tasks. item.title: Simple features beat control monitors
item.description: A word-counting classifier outscores most AI control monitors on the standard backdoor dataset, a living meta-analysis finds human-AI teams still do not beat the better member, and hijack detectors with high AUROC mostly raise false alerts at realistic attack rates. Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

item.title: Shutdown on replay, rare failures and a model audit
item.description: ShutdownMod turns recorded agent trajectories into shutdown evaluations, finding agents that keep working even after verifying the request; an independent audit of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash; and ALE, a way to estimate very rare failure rates of fine-tuned models. item.title: Approvals an agent cannot give itself
item.description: I-HITL, a formal definition of human approval that a compromised agent cannot forge, with nine of ten models raising their own wallet cap; budgeted audits against reward hacking in GRPO; and a case for lifespan-calibrated external evaluation.
